text: ὁ Δεινόσαυρος ἀνοίγει τὸν σάκκον καὶ λαμβάνει ἐκ τοῦ σάκκου τὰ νομίσματα.
objects: a small woven flax sack, tan with a drawstring, soft and slightly wrinkled, sized to fit in Dinosaur’s hands.
five bright silver coins, flat and round with simple stamped designs, about the size of large buttons.
a merchant’s stall table of chalk-white wood with neat woven baskets and a blue-painted edge.
a round rustic loaf of bread with a golden-brown crust and a cross-slashed top, about the size of Dinosaur’s head.
a basket of red apples, glossy and firm, heaped in a shallow wicker tray.
a tall clay water jar, terracotta with a simple blue band near the shoulder.
artist_notes: Slight push-in on hands, but keep both faces readable for emotion.
positioning: Dinosaur stands at the stall’s edge, front three-quarter view, looking down into his sack as he opens it.
Emporos waits behind the table, gentle smile, eyes on the coins and Dinosaur’s hands.
The small woven sack is open at chest height in Dinosaur’s hands.
The five bright silver coins glint in Dinosaur’s right hand just above the sack’s mouth.
The merchant’s stall table remains in front of Emporos, edge close to Dinosaur.
The round rustic loaf is still in its basket within easy reach, foreground right.
The basket of red apples remains piled beside the bread.
The tall clay water jar stands steady near the table’s back corner.
